description: A per-user reward-accrual lifecycle is broken by an omitted state reset/update: a dirty/stale flag, a per-user reward checkpoint, or a reward debt/index is set on one path but never cleared/advanced on recovery, so a validly-participating user permanently (or until an abnormal action like unstake+restake) stops accruing or cannot claim owed rewards. Anchored on the Munchables 2024-07 H-05 case (dirty flag set in _farmPlots, never reset in transferToUnoccupiedPlot -> permanent reward loss on a valid plot).

poc_level_descriptors.L3A: a participant is in a valid reward-earning state; trigger the path that sets the dirty/stale flag (or skips the checkpoint update)
poc_level_descriptors.L3B: restore the valid state (e.g. move to a valid plot / re-lock / re-enter); assert the flag/checkpoint is NOT reset (read the storage slot before/after)
poc_level_descriptors.L3C: assert the participant accrues 0 (or strictly less than the recoverable baseline) / cannot claim owed reward, and that no normal later action recovers it (only unstake+restake / abnormal action does)

high_severity_rationale: High requires proving the reward loss is permanent / not recoverable by a normal later action (only an abnormal action such as unstake+restake recovers it) AND quantifying the lost reward or the blocked claim path. Medium is proven by showing accrual is halted and the flag/checkpoint is not reset, without a permanence/quantified-loss proof. NOTE: a bounded/lazy reward mismatch that self-corrects on the next normal claim is NOT this class -> route to Low via the severity gate (P86).
negative_control_template: Reset the dirty/stale flag to false (or advance the per-user reward checkpoint / clear the reward debt) on the recovery path (e.g. inside transferToUnoccupiedPlot / on re-entry), and set lastRewardDate to block.timestamp. Assert the participant resumes accruing the recoverable baseline and can claim owed reward, with no other change.
